review_description: I had the solar panels installed 6 years ago & a 15kw battery last week, the men were very helpful & the system works fine, I highly recommend Space Solar.

My roof top solar system, installed by Space Solar, recently suffered a catastrophic failure. It was still under the 10 year warranty, but Space Solar refused to fix it. I had a qualified, independent inspector perform an audit which found 2 non-compliant installation-related issues. One of them caused the system failure, the other one has compromised equipment and potentially voided the manufacturers warranty for these components. I put in a warranty claim with Space Solar for the cost of fixing issue 1 and rectifying issue 2. They have refused to do either.They have been a nightmare to deal with and provably deliver non-compliant, sub-standard work - I have included a few snippets from the report.Do NOT use them.

The quoting process was very quick and efficient.Good installation. Made extra effort for the configuration we wanted. They helped organise the grid connection after the install and assisted with the set up of the Fnonius App (persisting when it had initial problems).

2017 Nov : I purchased a SolarEdge system from Space Solar. They quoted 1 day to install, but took 2 days. They also disconnected my TV antenna cable by accident without knowing, then denied that they did it.2023 Aug : One of the solar panels stopped generating. I contacted Space Solar for service. They quoted $330 for an inspection. When I mentioned my consumer rights (Fair Trading Act 1987 NSW), they changed their mind and quoted $550.2023 Sep 22 : I filed a complain with Fair Trading NSW. As a result, Space Solar told Fair Trading that they would come inspect for $330 instead of $550. Fair Trading also told me that, when they queried Space Solar on how did they come up with $550, the person at Space Solar could not give them an answer. I proceeded to file this matter in NCAT.2023 Nov 15 : Group hearing at NCAT Parramatta. Space Solar did not send any representative to the hearing. The tribunal adjourned the hearing and have it re-listed for second and final hearing.2024 Jan 16 : Hearing at NCAT Parramatta. Space Solar did not send any representative to the hearing again. The member of the tribunal decided to proceed with the hearing. The outcome was, the tribunal issued an order, that Space Solar would pay me a cash compensation in order to cover the cost of another installer coming to repair my solar panel.Would you like to buy something, anything, let alone a solar system, from a business which not only breaks the law on your consumer rights, but who doesn't even turn up to a tribunal hearing?

I spent 5 years to make a decision on Solar. Initially the solar panels were generating 200+ kw so the number of panels would have been 35+ panels. The roof real estate would have impacted the view from some of the bedrooms to which I concluded that until the panels generated more than 400+ kw, it was not to my liking.Buying a solar system requires research which one can otain by speaking companies in the 3 Solar Quote system.The Sales professionals overall are quite experienced and each one can help a buyer decide what is best for them.I learned about various roof construction,house positioning relative to North and West, shading possibility, Inverter capacity and location and ultimately the cost once you have decided on the size of the system.The additional requirements of a smart meter, the ability for the home to accomodate the additional solar circuit and the charges from the Electrcity supplier to accept the feed in, should be known before the final decision to go solar.Based on current costs per kwh of $0.27 kwh and what you Sell your electrcity back to the Supplier at $0.07 kwh, The payback is likey to be a minimum of 7 years.Should the Electricity suppliers continue their ever increasing rates will lowering the Sell back to them, the payback will be lower than 7 years but still an overall greater cost to the Solar user.

Ours was not and I was told that I was the first person to have requested it so Enphase wasn't sure if it would work. However, on that day I was informed that as of 01/12/17 Origin had changed its policy regarding net meters so that Space Solar could not do it and I had to apply to Origin for it to be done.I did phone Origin on 21/12/17 but they required an application form to be completed.  This form proved to have been designed for another purpose so it took some time to figure out how to fill it in to their satisfaction.  On 18/01/18 Origin confirmed they had raised a reference number for their subsidiary Acumen to change my metering setup and complete the work within 30 business days (which would be before 2/03/18).  That day came and went and eventually Acumen did the metering work on 11/04/18 (Day 167).Meanwhile I had to choose a new electricity supply plan.  I chose Origin's Solar Boost Plan which gave a 15 cent/kWh feed in tariff.  Origin has a plan that gives 17 cents/kWh but only if Origin does the solar installation.Satisfaction:	Space Solar	HighOrigin		LowReading the new meter	Complex

It's worth talking to as many suppliers as you can make time for.  Some will be pushy and try and sign you on the first contact - these are generally the ones that will cost more and are best avoided.  The more relaxed and interactive the supplier is, the easier they will be to work with.  Look for common brands and ideas amongst all the potential suppliers, consensus indicates believability.Do not be afraid to request a requote on a different configuration.  If your research suggests something different will suit you better, a reliable supplier will happily quote on whatever you want, while providing advice if they really believe you are making a mistake.  Most will use aerial photography to plan your installation but these can be out of date.  Check your roof against the shadows shown by the photography - in my case recent storms had blown down several trees that had removed shade from part of the roof, making it available when the photos showed it as shaded.Do your research on brands of panels, inverters and installation arrangements.  Read as much as you can.  It seems confusing at first but, again, common themes emerge and you can have confidence in those.It's very competitive out there at the moment, so it's a good time to get going with solar.

So they removed the panels already in place & fitted earthing cables. So far we have generated 11kWh in the week since installation - not bad as the panels are in dappled shade until around 13:30 and these are the shortest days of the year. Should get more power as the days get longer & the sun gets higher.One thing I hadn't realized until I discussed it with the Installer - a 1.5kW system will produce less than 1.5kW of power due to losses in the cabling & also when the cells warm above 25 degrees Celsius.For example my Trina panels are rated at 250 watts at STC - i.e. 25 degrees Celsius but when working in full sunlight the cells warm up to 42 degrees Celsius & the panel then only provides 185 watts.
